body:
### What happened

In hearsay-tools/cezarion, a comment-only edit to a shared test kit (`packages/cezar/src/workflows/waits-parity.testkit.ts`) selected 218 affected unit test files (plus 90 browser E2E files that were not counted). From the first `squeal status --wait` at that revision (2026-11-04T10:12:42Z) to the last named wait 1,252.5 s later, only 47 of the 218 unit files had a current verdict, all passing. 171 were still pending, and none were unknown or failed.

`runner.tierSize` is 4 in `squeal.config.json`. The admitted tiers held 4, 27 and 44 files. For the 27-file tier, wall time was 594.8 s and the summed file execution time was 587.3 s, so it ran at about 0.99 effective workers. The 44-file tier ran at about 0.97. On this host the repository's Vitest `maxWorkers` resolves to 14 (24 CPUs, 28.8 GB free), and the unit projects do not set `fileParallelism: false`. So the serial execution does not come from the repository's Vitest settings. Named waits were promoted, but the active tier did not yield to them.

The repository's own CI runs all 1,388 Vitest files in four shards, with no file at or above 40 s (run 41813391250). The local verdict latency is therefore set by tier execution, not by test file length.

### What you expected

A large tier should run its files in parallel, up to the configured Vitest worker count, so that verdicts for the affected files arrive within the per-file cap plus a short delay. A named wait should get its file run soon even while a large tier is active.

### Command and output

`squeal status --wait 60000 <named files>` repeated from 10:12:42Z. Summary of the recorded measurement:

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit files selected | 218 (90 browser files excluded) |
| Current pass after 1,252.5 s | 47 |
| Pending after 1,252.5 s | 171 |
| Unknown or failed | 0 |
| Execution time per file, median / p90 | 20.5 s / 34.5 s |
| Run-admission queue delay, median / p90 (lower bound) | 213.1 s |
| First wait to verdict, median / p90 | 809.0 s |
| Effective workers in the 27- and 44-file tiers | about 0.99 / 0.97 |
| Projected time for all 218 at the observed rate | about 97 min |
| Load average at start / end (24 CPUs) | 16.6 / 37.0 |

### Squeal version

0.1.390 (the Codex session pin; the Claude Code plugin was 0.1.392).

### Squeal revision

13.

### Harness

Codex.

### Model

gpt-6.1-sol-fast.

### Cost

About 21 minutes of waiting with no verdict for 171 files. The repository's planned removal of its Squeal wait bound (hearsay-tools/cezarion#2519) is blocked on this measurement, so agents keep a manual fallback.

### Did a daemon restart clear it?

Not tried during the measurement window; the measurement needed one continuous daemon.

### Suggested fix

Run the files of an admitted tier in parallel, up to the runner's worker count, and record the granted worker count per tier in status. Let a named wait preempt or join an active large tier. Related, but not the same: hearsay-tools/squeal#127 (fast retry waits behind tiers) and hearsay-tools/squeal#110 (ordering of named slow files).
title: Admitted tiers execute at about one effective worker, so a shared test-kit edit takes over an hour to get verdicts
